learningObjective: Explain GPTQ's central technique: per-layer weight quantization via second-order (Hessian-inverse-based) error compensation.

canonicalClaims.claim: GPTQ quantizes weights one column at a time, using the Cholesky-inverse of the layer's Hessian (H ≈ 2 X^T X from calibration activations) to update the still-unquantized columns and compensate for each newly-introduced quantization error. It is a per-layer, offline PTQ method (no full model retraining).
conditions: The layer is a linear layer with a computable Hessian.
A calibration activation set is available.
nonImplications: Does not imply GPTQ handles activation outliers — it focuses on weight quantization; typical deployment is W4A16.
Does not imply GPTQ is universally optimal — AWQ and RTN are alternatives with different trade-offs.

misconceptions.claim: GPTQ is a form of QAT: it retrains the model with STE on quantized weights.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPTQ is PTQ; it performs no full-model training, only per-layer weight optimization against calibration activations.

misconceptions.claim: GPTQ uses reinforcement learning to search for quantization scales.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPTQ uses a closed-form second-order weight update, not RL.

misconceptions.claim: GPTQ is a runtime dequantization technique that speeds up INT4 → FP16 conversion.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPTQ is an offline quantization algorithm; the runtime dequant kernel is a separate concern (e.g., Marlin, ExLlama).

misconceptions.claim: The Hessian used by GPTQ is the full model Hessian.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPTQ uses the per-layer Hessian of the layer's reconstruction error, which is O((in_features)^2) and tractable.

implementationFacts: GPTQ's per-layer cost is dominated by the Cholesky inverse of the Hessian; typical LLaMA-7B takes minutes on a single GPU.
Standard deployment: W4A16 with per-group scales (group_size 128).
performanceScenarios: GPT-3 175B with GPTQ INT4 W4A16: perplexity increase of ~1-4% vs FP16 with 4× weight compression.
